reuse.why: Puts the daily-skip rule into the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and threads frequency through parseRecurDate, so every site reuses the shared helper; the template site adds a small local wrapper rather than a shared one.

duplication.why: Each site re-solves 'look further ahead because occurrences may be skipped' its own way (WEEKEND_LOOKAHEAD in getNextDate, count*7 plus filter/slice in getUpcomingDates, null-aware loop in templates), and getUpcomingDates re-encodes the 'daily' predicate to size its lookahead.

placement.why: The weekend rule stays in shared/schedules.ts and frequency is carried on the parsed schedule data where weekend settings already live; the lookahead handling is necessarily at call sites.

scope.why: All edits serve the daily-skip rule, with focused tests.

maintainability.why: Changing the helper's return to Date | null is a reasonable contract, but the per-site lookahead heuristics and the duplicated 'daily' check in getUpcomingDates would need to move together if the rule changed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All three date sites still go through getDateWithSkippedWeekend; getUpcomingDates' isSkippingDaily only sizes the lookahead.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-aware lookahead is re-implemented in three shapes (constant take of 7 in getNextDate, count*7 + filter + slice in getUpcomingDates, null-guarded counting loop in createScheduleList), and getUpcomingDates repeats the frequency === 'daily' predicate the helper owns.

one_place.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts decides daily-skip vs move for getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and createScheduleList (caveat: getUpcomingDates also checks frequency === 'daily' to size its lookahead).
